verdict: Costco's sales rose 11.2% in its 16-week fourth quarter — and the $1.9B of membership fees it collected covered nearly two-thirds of its entire net profit.

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold in 939 warehouses and online — comparable sales up 9.4% (6.7% adjusted for gasoline prices and currency).

segments.name: Membership fees
segments.note: Annual membership fees — almost pure profit, and the heart of the business model: members pay to shop, then spend heavily.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the warehouses and the company — just 8.8% of revenue, famously lean.

takeaways.title: Shoppers keep coming
takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 9.4% (6.7% excluding gasoline-price and currency swings), and digitally-enabled sales grew 19.5%. Net sales hit $93.9B in the 16-week quarter.

takeaways.title: The membership is the profit
takeaways.text: Membership fees of $1,850M covered 62% of the quarter's $2,998M net income. Costco can price goods close to cost because members pay an annual fee just to walk in.

takeaways.title: A tariff refund helped
takeaways.text: EPS included a non-recurring +$0.15 per share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, partly reinvested in member prices. Even without it, EPS of about $6.60 would still be up roughly 12%.

oneTimers: A non-recurring benefit of $0.15 per diluted share from IEEPA tariff refunds received in the quarter, net of amounts reinvested in lower prices and member values.
otherDetail: Interest income and other of $253M, less $45M of interest expense — net +$208M.
footerNote: Costco's fourth quarter is 16 weeks (the others are 12), so it is not directly comparable to a normal quarter.
